newsitem.title: USA: Ford sees Q4 results higher than year-ago.
newsitem.headline: Ford sees Q4 results higher than year-ago.

text.p: Ford Motor Co, experiencing an earnings rebound, expects to report fourth quarter profits that are up from the $660 million income of a year ago, Senior Vice President of Finance David McCammon said Wednesday.
"Going forward, the fourth quarter we expect will show a profit improvement over the prior year," McCammon told reporters during a news briefing at Ford's headquarters.
Responding to losses in Europe, McCammon said Ford is launching a broad plan to cut costs that will include reviewing product, material, personnel and plant expenses.

In the third quarter, Ford earned a net profit of $686 million, up from a profit of $357 million a year ago. The earnings were hurt by losses from Europe, which grew to $472 million from a loss of $320 million in the 1995 third quarter.

McCammon said Ford Chairman Alex Trotman has left to visit operations in Europe and other executives will soon follow. Ford has passed through its high-volume product launches, which will give it new offerings, but now must take a look at costs, he said.

"I think the product part of that will show substantial improvement, and there will be actions taken on the cost front as well," he said. "When will that turn around? I don't know, I hope by next year it will have turned around."

McCammon said Ford expects its fourth quarter U.S. retail incentives to continue to be at high levels, although overall marketing costs as a percentage of sales will not be as high. Ford spent an average of $1,100 per vehicle on U.S. retail incentives in the third quarter, up from $850 a year ago.

Ford will amortize the cost of the $2,000 lump-sum payment it paid to its United Auto Workers earlier in October as part of a new contract over the next 12 months, McCammon said. He said the new labor pact will increase Ford's labor costs by four to five percent, not unlike prior agreements.

Separately, McCammon said Ford expects total U.S. industry vehicle sales to be about 15.4 million for the second half of 1996, lower than 15.6 million in the first half but on track for a total year selling rate of about 15.5 million.
